_about: What the neatline tool cannot find, written by the person checking (charts/neatline.py). A side is a meridian or parallel in degrees, or "file" for a side that runs on to the edge of the sheet. A cut is a ring in the file's pixels (col, row): an inset or panel printed over the chart's body; inside the body it is a hole, across its edge it notches it. Each says why.

green-bay-sec.why: North runs on into Ontario to the edge of the sheet, with no sectional beyond it. East meets Lake Huron's west neatline; the tool leaves it open because Lake Huron's sheet stops 0.1 degree short of Green Bay's in the north.

halifax-sec.why: North and east run on to the edges of the sheet (Quebec, the Gulf of Saint Lawrence, the Atlantic), with no sectional beyond them.

lake-huron-sec.why: North runs on into Ontario to the edge of the sheet, and east on past Montreal's west neatline (-77) to the edge of the sheet. Canada is printed in pale grey, which the tool took for margin.

miami-sec.why: North meets Jacksonville's south neatline; above 28 the sheet's east half is margin with notes. East runs on over the Bahamas to the edge of the sheet.

montreal-sec.why: North runs on into Quebec to the edge of the sheet, with no sectional beyond it. West is the -77 meridian, where the body ends; the tool, finding Lake Huron's east side open too, took each from the other.

new-york-sec.why: North meets the south neatlines of Montreal and Halifax, which the tool would not join because Halifax overlaps it by only 0.35 degree. East runs on over the Atlantic to the edge of the sheet.

phoenix-sec.why: South runs on into Sonora to the edge of the sheet. A quarter degree inside it (31.5) would lose Arizona south of it, Nogales and Douglas included. North, the body ends on the scale bars' straight edge (35.70 at the ends, 35.747 in the middle), not on 35.75: it meets Las Vegas and Denver at 35.6875, inside all three bodies.

las-vegas-sec.why: The body ends on the scale bars' straight edge (35.58 to 35.635). South is lowered to Phoenix's north, 35.6875, so the two overlap and no ruler shows.

denver-sec.why: The body ends on the scale bars' straight edge (35.58 to 35.636). South is lowered to Phoenix's north, 35.6875, so the two overlap and no ruler shows.

jacksonville-sec.why: Two insets at a larger scale: one in the north-east corner, over the Atlantic, and one over the Gulf west of Tampa.

los-angeles-sec.why: The legend's column reaches into the body's north-west corner, and the Los Angeles inset covers the south-west, over the Pacific. The ground elevations bar beside the legend's column, printed over the Pacific, goes with it.

new-orleans-sec.why: A diagram of the restricted airspace at Eglin and Pensacola, printed over the Gulf at another scale.

washington-sec.why: The Norfolk inset, printed over the Atlantic and across the body's east edge.

chicago-hel.why: The tool found no frame line along the left; this is the left frame's rule, measured by hand.

new-york-hel.why: The body is stepped, not four-sided: a lobe reaches north from its top, and a block of text takes its south-west corner. Its ten frame rules, traced and fitted straight (within half a pixel), and their corners.

seattle-tac.why: The bottom frame is a parallel (46.75), bowed 13 pixels from straight over its length, so no straight line fits it. The four sides traced: three straight, the bottom as an arc.

colorado-springs-tac.why: The ground elevations panel, printed over the body against its left frame: cut from the frame out.
